_doc: Chunk 2.2 (finding D2-05). Series rendered by window_data.js with NO row in master, long_master, extraction_output/staging or extractions. regenerate_ui_data.py deep-copies any curated variable with no master ID match from the PRIOR window_data.js, so a series extracted once and later retired renders forever with nothing behind it. These ids are stripped from the payload on every rebuild. REVERSIBLE: delete an id from this file and re-run regenerate_ui_data.py; if a source later appears, extract it and the id returns through the normal master path.

pres_has_gobernador.reason:
Withdrawn on the owner's instruction, 2026-08-04, after the v2-close session found it. The series carries NO INFORMATION. Every one of its published cells is the value 1 — 329 cells across 50 departments and 20 years, 1855 to 1908 — and master holds 332 rows with the same single distinct value and not one zero anywhere. The definition promises `1 if the department had a Gobernador, 0 otherwise`, but the 0 branch never occurs, so the indicator cannot distinguish `had one` from `no record was made` and a choropleth of it is a map of one colour. What it actually measures is which departments appear in the Presupuesto line items that were extracted, which is a coverage artefact and not a measure of state reach.

149 of the master rows are additionally `[v1_hygiene_attributed=2026-05-18;basis=primary_sibling_backfill]`, a value copied from a sibling year rather than read from a budget, so part of the constant is inferred rather than observed.

NO GATE COULD SEE THIS. G6 finds no magnitude step in a constant, G1b passes because the rows are `observed`, G4 passes because the citation and definition are present, and G5 passes because the series does render. It took reading the values.

REVERSIBLE and NOT a deletion: all 332 master rows are untouched and still ship in the CSV download. Remove this entry to republish. The series becomes publishable the day the 0 cases are extracted — a department present in the budget WITHOUT a Gobernador is the observation that makes the binary meaningful.

_not_withdrawn_reconstructed_by_curation._note: These carry no master row under their own name, so 2.1 classified them unattributable, but scripts/apply_curation_15_reconstructed_series.py DERIVES them from primary master inputs and runs AFTER this withdrawal. Withdrawing them therefore does not stick, and should not: a documented reconstruction from primary data is provenance. Listing them here rather than under 'withdraw', because a register that claims a withdrawal which does not happen is the same class of silent divergence this repair exists to remove. Caveat carried forward: these are the tax-share series recorded as laundered DLW; curation 15 reconstructs them from primary inputs, but that reconstruction has not been re-audited here.

_constant_binary_note_2026_08_04: pres_has_gobernador and pres_has_juez withdrawn on the owner's instruction. Both are binary presence indicators whose 0 branch never occurs, so they published a constant 1 over 672 cells between them. Worth carrying as a CLASS: a 0/1 indicator with no zeros is measuring extraction coverage, not the thing it names, and none of the eight gates can detect it. If another binary indicator reaches the catalog, check its value distribution before exposing it.
_p1a_note_2026_08_05: 30 ids withdrawn because the P1a concept merge renamed them IN MASTER into the canonical recorded as `merged_into`. Their cells are not lost: they sit under the canonical id, which publishes. Withdrawal is the right mechanism rather than concept_aliases.json, because an alias merges two LIVE series and the alias register correctly refused (both `births_male` and `nacimientos_hombres` were published, so merging would arbitrate values). Here the old id is dead in master, so it must stop rendering. REVERSIBLE: delete an id and rebuild.
